messages:
casey_support: Hey team — customer 'novacare' flagged their dashboard showing intermittent negative and zero spikes for streaming TTFT / tokens/sec over the last ~2h. Screenshot attached: https://files.redwood.example/novacare-ttft-ghosts.png :thinking_face:

maria: saw that alert too. grafana panel shows brief -1.2 then back to normal. windows look 10s aggregated. not seeing errors in the hosted API logs for this customer.

jonathan_sre: Can you paste the query timeframe? Also checking kafka consumer offsets + aggregator logs. Negative deltas usually mean a rollup snapshot produced a smaller cumulative counter (out-of-order or checkpoint reset).

casey_support: Time range 2026-03-16T08:45Z -> 2026-03-16T10:15Z. Customer is worried because billing dashboard uses the same pipeline. They've opened a support ticket, escalating.

alex_infra: quick check: could be a consumer replay/compaction causing counters to go backward. Running a quick logs grep:

```
kubectl logs -l app=metrics-collector -c consumer --since=2h | grep -E "novacare|token_rate" -A 3
"2026-03-16T09:12:05Z consumer.go:278] customer=novacare partition=3 offset=491202: emit rollup delta -12.0 tokensec (prev_sum=1204.0 cur_sum=1192.0)"
```

jonathan_sre: that log line is the smoking gun — aggregator emitted a negative delta. Immediate questions: did we see a consumer group rebalance / offset reset around that timestamp? Check kafka-consumer-groups and the commit logs.

metrics-bot: ALERT: streaming.metric.token_rate negative value detected for customer=novacare at 2026-03-16T09:12:05Z. Incident ID: METRICS-4821.

maria: I pulled the consumer group state — there was a brief rebalance at 09:11:58Z for group metrics-collector-prod which coincides with the negative delta. Might be race between checkpoint persist and rollup checkpointing.

jonathan_sre: repro steps I'm going to run: replay ~2k raw events around that partition offset to see ordering and timestamps. Command I will run locally:

```
kafka-console-consumer --bootstrap-server kafka.redwood:9092 --topic streaming-tokens --partition 3 --offset 491180 --max-messages 400 \
  | jq -r '. | "offset=\(.offset) ts=\(.timestamp) sum=\(.cumulative_sum)"' > /tmp/novacare-window-replay.log
```

alex_infra: short-term mitigation: clamp negative rollup deltas to 0 at emit time so dashboards and billing don't see negatives. I'll push a canary to us-west-2 with that guard. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/metrics/PR-9487 :hammer_and_wrench:

casey_support: please confirm ETA for canary and whether this changes billing numbers. Customer is asking for corrective backfill.

jonathan_sre: ETA: canary in ~20m, monitor for 30m. If stable we'll promote. For backfill, plan is to replay and recompute rollups for novacare partition(s) for the last 6h and re-ingest to the analytics index. I can run the backfill script once canary proves stable. Backfill script (devops):

```
python tools/recompute_rollups.py --customer novacare --start "2026-03-16T04:00:00Z" --end "2026-03-16T10:30:00Z" --partitions 3
```

maria: note: we should also add a regression test to assert monotonic counters and a metrics-lint that rejects negative deltas on CI for the collector. Filing follow-up: METRICS-4822.

alex_infra: canary deployed to us-west-2 (canary-id=canary-2026-03-16-09-35). Will post results in 30m.

casey_support: thanks — pinging customer with interim note: "We're aware, mitigation in progress, will follow up with timeline for backfill and billing impact."

jonathan_sre: update: after canary clamp, dashboards show no negative spikes in the same window. Still verifying that clamping doesn't hide an upstream data-loss bug. Next steps: 1) complete backfill, 2) investigate consumer rebalance cause (possible ZK/coordination hiccup), 3) add safeguards + alerting to prevent billing exposure.

casey_support: marking high priority. I'll update ticket MET-72614 and loop in account manager.

metrics-bot: NOTE: scheduled backfill job queued METRICS-4821-BF, owner=jonathan_sre, eta=3h.

maria: leaving this thread once backfill completes, will follow to close regression ticket.

casey_support: final note for record — root cause suspected: transient consumer group rebalance causing an out-of-order checkpoint commit which produced a lower cumulative counter; mitigation: clamp negative deltas + recompute rollups for affected windows.
